description: Development split used while tuning prompts (python -m evals.run_evals --golden evals/dev.json). It is kept separate from golden.json so the reported golden-set numbers are not tuned on directly. Same format and scoring as golden.json.

cases.question: Show the 5 most recent orders with the customer's first and last name.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT o.OrderDate, c.FirstName, c.LastName FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC LIMIT 5
cases.notes: Compared as a set: several of the 5 orders share a date.

cases.question: How many employees were hired in each year?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', HireDate) AS HireYear, COUNT(*) AS Hires FROM Employees GROUP BY HireYear

cases.question: Which product categories have an average unit price above $200?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT Category FROM Products GROUP BY Category HAVING AVG(UnitPrice) > 200

cases.question: Which employees don't have a manager?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE ManagerID IS NULL

cases.question: What was the total amount paid by credit card in 2025?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) AS TotalPaid FROM Payments WHERE PaymentMethod = 'Credit Card' AND PaymentDate >= '2025-01-01' AND PaymentDate < '2026-01-01'

cases.question: Which department has the highest total salary cost?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT d.DepartmentName FROM Employees AS e JOIN Departments AS d ON d.DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID GROUP BY d.DepartmentName ORDER BY SUM(e.Salary) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What is the average order value for each customer segment in 2025?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.Segment, ROUND(AVG(o.TotalAmount), 2) AS AvgOrderValue FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2025-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY c.Segment

cases.question: How many customers placed orders in both 2024 and 2025?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Customers FROM Customers AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders AS o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID AND o.OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2025-01-01') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders AS o WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID AND o.OrderDate >= '2025-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-01-01')

cases.question: Which products are currently out of stock?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ProductName FROM Products WHERE StockQuantity = 0

cases.question: How many former employees are there?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS FormerEmployees FROM Employees WHERE IsActive = 0

turns: Sort them by stock, highest first, and show only the top 5.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT ProductName FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice < 50 ORDER BY StockQuantity DESC LIMIT 5

turns: Who are the top 5 customers by total order amount?
Now only count orders placed in 2024.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName, c.LastName FROM Customers AS c JOIN Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY SUM(o.TotalAmount) DESC LIMIT 5

turns: Group them by month and count them.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Orders FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2025-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', OrderDate)
cases.notes: Only the counts are compared; the month label format is free.

turns: List the employees in the Sales department.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName, e.Salary FROM Employees AS e JOIN Departments AS d ON d.DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID WHERE d.DepartmentName = 'Sales'

turns: Show customers from Texas in the Corporate segment.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Customers WHERE State = 'Texas'
cases.notes: 'Remove the ... filter' edits the query; it is not a destructive request.

cases.question: Fix this query: SELEC FirstName, LastName FORM Employees WHERE Salary > 100000
cases.gold_sql: SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE Salary > 100000
